landing.headline: Learn to Cast and Read The I Ching
levelDescriptions: Ask a question and get the traditional answer from The Book of Change.
Learn how to calculate the hexagrams and how to interpret the answers.
Ask questions, learn intuitively and apply the results to a specific situation.

what.heading: One of The Oldest Books and Divination Methods in The World
what.body: Its Chinese name, Yìjīng 易經, means "the Classic of Changes." At its core are 64 figures of six lines, each with a short text, compiled in China close to three thousand years ago. For most of its life it has been two things at once: a way to consult on decisions that mattered, and a book of philosophy about how change moves through nature and through a life.

yesNo.heading: Are You Sure?
yesNo.lead: The I Ching doesn't answer yes or no.
yesNo.body: It describes the situation you're in and the stance it asks of you: to move, to wait, to yield, to persist. You can keep your question as it is, or open it up a little.
yesNo.example: Instead of "Should I take the job?", try "What should I understand about taking this job?"
